issues.legal_issue: Cancellation of an allotment under the statutory power requires a finding that the allotment was obtained through fraud, false representation, or concealment of a material fact.
material_facts: A company received an allotment of replacement land based on a registered sale deed for land it said it had owned before partition.
The authority rejected the deed and found that the company had not proved ownership or occupation of the original land, describing the allotment as undeserved.
The authority cancelled the allotment without finding that it had been obtained through fraud, false representation, or concealment of a material fact.
issues.conclusion: The cancellation order was quashed because the authority had no jurisdiction to cancel the allotment without the required finding; the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 24(2) of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, a finding that an allotment was obtained by fraud, false representation, or concealment of a material fact is a mandatory condition precedent to cancellation. A finding that the recipient failed to prove title, or that the allotment was undeserved, is not equivalent to that finding. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.allotment_cancellation_proceeding: An authority acted to cancel a displaced person's allotment of replacement property.
predicates.no_procurement_misconduct_finding: The authority made no finding that the allotment had been obtained through fraud, false representation, or concealment of a material fact.
predicates.cancellation_order_is_without_jurisdicti: The cancellation order is beyond the authority's jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When an authority acts to cancel a displaced person's allotment and makes no finding of procurement misconduct, the cancellation order is without jurisdiction.
